source_level_article_analyses.title: Bank capital, lending, and regulation: A meta-analysis

jif.verification: Wiley journal metrics / publisher journal page (current metric safely above project floor)

full_text.source: Wiley version plus publicly attached author/published full-text copies at university repositories
full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: construct meta-analytic evidence universe of 1,600+ estimates
separate capital-ratio levels from changes in capital requirements
close with limits on policy-ready effect-size claims
rhetoric.evidence_order: The review separates the relationship between bank capital levels and lending from the effect of changes in regulatory requirements before synthesizing moderators and publication bias.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Effect sizes matter because the sign/magnitude differ by the exact capital construct. Numbers establish that level relationships and regulatory-change effects are not interchangeable.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Meta-analysis supports pooled associations/effects conditional on underlying designs; it does not turn heterogeneous primary studies into one structural mechanism.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Post-crisis period, capital definition, empirical method, and regulatory context materially change estimates.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: A literature can have a directional pooled result and still fail to provide a sufficiently stable effect size for policy calibration.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Bank-capital ratio, regulatory capital ratio, and changes in capital requirements are related but distinct constructs across heterogeneous studies.
rhetoric.limitations: Publication bias, modeling choices, time variation, and primary-study design heterogeneity bound policy generalization.
rhetoric.implications: Finance summaries should not use 'more bank capital' and 'higher capital requirements' as grammatical substitutes when the evidence shows different lending relationships.
anti_patterns: Do not collapse a level variable and a policy-induced change into one financial condition.
Do not treat a pooled average as policy-ready when study design materially determines estimates.

atomic_observations.observation: A variable's level and an imposed change in that variable are different evidentiary objects and can have different or opposite relationships with outcomes; prose should not treat them as interchangeable.
A literature can support a broad directional relationship while remaining too heterogeneous to supply a reliable policy effect size.
Finance language should distinguish bank capital levels, regulatory ratios, capital requirements, and changes in requirements.
Meta-analytic synthesis should decompose capital constructs and empirical contexts before stating an aggregate lending conclusion.

summary_architecture: define competition between working and fixed capital for cash
rhetoric.evidence_order: The paper establishes the cash-allocation mechanism before using heterogeneous working-capital needs and liquidity to test whether the proposed channel behaves as predicted.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: The useful magnitude comparison is short-term versus long-term constraint importance; subgroup effects show when internal liquidity absorbs the shock.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The mechanism is supported by predicted heterogeneity but hidden treatment-selection bias cannot be completely ruled out; mechanism wording should remain calibrated to the design.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Higher working-capital needs amplify the investment effect; liquid firms that can adjust receivables/inventories are less exposed.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: The article separates cash-credit and investment-credit constraints rather than treating any finance denial as the same event.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: French SME/manufacturing-heavy survey setting; treatment assignment can contain unobserved factors; unquoted firms require accounting proxies.
rhetoric.limitations: Authors explicitly note non-representative sector composition and inability to guarantee absence of hidden bias.
rhetoric.implications: Internal liquidity is not merely a balance-sheet stock: it can function as a buffer that lets firms meet working-capital needs without sacrificing fixed investment.
anti_patterns: Do not describe all credit constraints as equivalent when short- and long-term finance serve competing uses.
Do not state the working-capital channel more strongly than the identification permits.

atomic_observations.observation: Finance prose can describe working capital and fixed investment as competing uses of finite internal cash, making allocation pressure explicit.
Liquidity changes the strength of the financing-constraint effect; the buffer condition belongs in the interpretation.
Predicted moderator behavior can support a mechanism without fully identifying it.
Hidden-bias and sample-composition limits should be attached to the causal/channel claim they constrain.

full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: define guarantee intervention and business-continuity outcomes
rhetoric.evidence_order: Profitability and financial-health outcomes are kept separate, then followed through time before policy interpretation.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: The meaningful quantitative structure is outcome divergence and decay of financial burdens over time, not a single average treatment-effect number.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Causal language is most justified for the matched difference-in-differences treatment effects and should remain outcome-specific.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Micro/small firms, services, and direct guarantees show larger magnitudes; financial burdens weaken by year two.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: The paper refuses a simple good/bad judgment: profitability improves while short-run financial equilibrium worsens.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Italian guarantee program, 2010–2018, uniform regulatory context; post-pandemic generalization remains untested.
rhetoric.limitations: Country/program/time boundaries are explicit; benefit-cost conclusions depend on beneficiary selection and intervention design.
rhetoric.implications: The same financing intervention can improve operating performance while temporarily worsening leverage and debt-service strain.
anti_patterns: Do not compress a multi-outcome intervention into 'helped' or 'hurt.'
Do not omit the recovery path when the short-run adverse effect fades.

atomic_observations.observation: An intervention can succeed on one financial objective and deteriorate another; evaluation must remain outcome-specific.
Short-run deterioration followed by medium-term relief should be stated as a time path.
Government-backed finance can be described through profitability additionality, leverage, financial burden, debt sustainability, and business-continuity tradeoffs.
Strong intervention verbs are justified only for outcomes supported by the quasi-experimental design.

source_level_article_analyses.title: Small and vulnerable during crises? Firm size and financing constraint dynamics

full_text.source: Springer Nature open-access full HTML
full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: separate pre-crisis constraint level from crisis-induced change
trace post-crisis deleveraging and cash accumulation
rhetoric.evidence_order: The article deliberately distinguishes being more constrained on average from being disproportionately worsened by the crisis.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Comparative differences in baseline probability and crisis interaction answer distinct questions; the paper avoids making size itself the sole vulnerability metric.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The crisis interaction can be interpreted more strongly than a simple cross-sectional level difference, but bank-side supply information is limited.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: SMEs have worse baseline financing conditions, yet the crisis did not tighten constraints disproportionately by size; constrained firms across sizes recover similarly.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: No disproportionate SME crisis effect is stated as a non-difference in shock response, not as evidence that SMEs are financially unconstrained.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Established German firms; very small/young firms underrepresented; bank-level financing supply cannot be directly linked.
rhetoric.limitations: Administrative detail comes with limited bank-side data and country/startup generalizability.
rhetoric.implications: Cash-buffer building is a post-shock financial adaptation and may substitute for debt even when the underlying firm population is otherwise similar.
anti_patterns: Do not infer shock sensitivity from a worse baseline.
Do not treat size as a complete explanation when risk characteristics and funding alternatives matter.

atomic_observations.observation: A group can have a worse baseline state without experiencing a larger response to a shock; level disparity and shock sensitivity are separate claims.
Crisis and post-crisis periods change the financing interpretation, so the temporal regime belongs in the claim.
Cash accumulation can be described as a financing buffer and potential substitute for debt during recovery.
The conclusion should retain the established-German-firm sample rather than becoming a universal SME claim.

full_text.source: Springer Nature open-access full HTML

summary_architecture: interact policy with leverage and risk measures
separate firm-perceived risk from size/age proxies
rhetoric.evidence_order: Policy stance comes first, then the article asks which firms actually experience easier finance; the answer is conditioned by jurisdiction, leverage, age, and size.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Interaction estimates are meaningful only with the firm/jurisdiction condition attached; broad asset-purchase measures are tested against alternatives.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The study identifies uneven transmission rather than proving a single bank risk-taking mechanism; firm risk measures and bank behavior are distinct evidentiary objects.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Leveraged firms in stressed countries, small firms, and young firms remain constrained; effects are insignificant in non-stressed countries and for several risk interactions.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: ‘Little evidence’ that risky firms receive loans under UMP is preserved rather than inverted into a statement that risk-taking never occurs.

atomic_observations.observation: Observed use of one financing channel depends on the supply and accessibility of alternatives; financing shares are jointly determined by need and channel availability.
Investment funding becomes interpretable when decomposed by source rather than summarized as one external-finance quantity.

Do not treat DPI and RVPI as interchangeable components of fund performance.
Do not evaluate cash-flow-sensitive performance with a metric that silently ignores timing.
Do not present an imputed performance estimate as an observed fund cash flow.

atomic_observations.observation: A headline performance measure becomes more informative when decomposed into cash contributed, cash distributed, residual value, timing, and benchmark-relative performance.
DPI is a realized-distribution object while RVPI is a residual/unrealized-value object; the two should survive compression even when both contribute to a broader total-value assessment.

Cash-flow timing matters to evaluation; a performance measure that uses later or missing information answers a different question from the information state actually available at an earlier decision point.
An imputed risk-adjusted return can be a useful operational estimate without becoming identical to the unobserved cash-flow history from which direct performance would be computed.

Do not make the supply-chain channel more causal than the observational design permits.

Finance prose can distinguish purchase orders/backlog, input procurement, fulfillment capacity, future sales recognition, and eventual profitability.

Backlog change can proxy purchase orders without being identical to every form of contracted demand.

A financing spread can contain distinct components whose responses differ; decomposition prevents a generic 'credit risk' story.

Finance language should distinguish short-term funding, long-term funding, rollover risk, liquidity creation, illiquid lending, and off-balance-sheet commitments.

A modeled target is an operational construct useful for dynamic analysis without being identical to a directly observed managerial target.

rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: The effect is stronger for financially constrained firms and where banks have greater monitoring/bargaining power; greater bank competition or more lender relationships attenuate the effect.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: Insignificant or weaker pre-trends/interaction components are retained as design and scope evidence rather than ignored.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: U.S. firms with debt-covenant information, 1995–2008; covenant breach is a contractual threshold and the study focuses on subsequent financial-reporting behavior rather than full economic default.

rhetoric.implications: Finance prose should distinguish covenant threshold, covenant violation, creditor control rights, bank intervention, financial constraint, lender bargaining power, and subsequent borrower behavior.

rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Observed spreads, matched/OLS estimates, potential-outcome estimates, and timing regressions are kept as different evidentiary objects.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The preferred estimates are counterfactual outputs of endogenous-treatment specifications; they are stronger than descriptive comparisons but remain conditional on the selection equations and instruments.

Do not generalize listed-firm estimates to firms without realistic bond-market access.

atomic_observations.observation: An observed between-group pricing difference and a modeled treatment effect are different estimands; endogenous selection can make the descriptive contrast materially smaller than the counterfactual effect.
Access to an alternative funding channel can change terms in another channel by altering outside options, not merely by substituting one funding source for another.
Counterfactual treatment estimates must be described as model-dependent potential outcomes and kept separate from observed spreads and simple matched-sample contrasts.
An information-release mechanism can receive partial support without exhausting the effect of continuing market access, bargaining power, or lender market power.

rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Additive return decomposition, a 65-paper measurement audit, bond-month overlap, filter reconciliation, pairwise correlations, serial-correlation tests, and lead-lag regressions answer separate questions.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The paper is a measurement and data-quality analysis, not a causal corporate-finance design; its strongest claims concern estimand contamination and observable vendor differences.

Do not equate a larger raw dataset with the economically relevant or synchronously measured universe.

atomic_observations.observation: When an observed return combines rate and credit components that covary negatively, using the aggregate measure can add noise or reverse inference about the target credit component.

Data-provider coverage defines a sample and economic target: more securities is not automatically broader relevant coverage when inclusion rules, liquidity, and instrument types differ.

long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: Define the private-equity contract and decompose commitment, calls/contributions, harvesting, and distributions.
structure: separate contribution and distribution cash flows
place them in a lifecycle while allowing overlap

observations.observation: Committed capital is an authorization or contractual ceiling, not paid-in cash; a capital call/contribution is a later transaction flow that draws against that commitment.
Private-capital prose should keep commitment, capital call, contribution, investment period, harvesting period, and distribution as distinct lifecycle objects.

Lifecycle stages are dominant timing patterns rather than perfectly disjoint boxes: distributions may begin before the investment period is fully over, so stage language should allow overlap when the evidence does.

long_form_passage_analyses.stylistic_notes: Define the contractual state before discussing cash-flow realization; use lifecycle language without implying hard stage boundaries unsupported by the source.

long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: Explain the J-curve and why timing uncertainty creates a liquidity-management problem.
structure: aggregate to cumulative net cash position
connect timing uncertainty to liquidity decision

observations.observation: Cumulative net cash position is built from distributions minus contributions; it should not be treated as interchangeable with DPI, RVPI, NAV, or a single-period cash flow.
Liquidity exposure depends on the timing and path of future calls and distributions, not only on the total committed amount; magnitude and timing are separate parts of the financing state.

long_form_passage_analyses.stylistic_notes: Move from component flows to the cumulative path, then to the decision consequence; do not use the J-curve as a substitute for the underlying cash-flow decomposition.

long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: Separate remaining commitment from the rate/path at which capital is drawn.

observations.observation: Remaining commitment is a stock/state while the drawdown or contribution rate describes the speed of movement through that state; the level and its adjustment velocity should be reported separately.

When a model imposes object-consistent constraints such as nonnegative remaining commitment, prose should preserve those constraints rather than narrate impossible states as if they were empirical possibilities.

long_form_passage_analyses.stylistic_notes: State variables first, flow dynamics second; keep mathematical constraints tied to the real-world object they encode.

structure: condition future path on realized observations

observations.observation: Contribution and distribution channels should be decomposed before aggregation because they represent opposite-direction cash-flow processes with different timing behavior.

A forecast or expected cash-flow path should update when new calls or distributions become known; revision after new information is analytically different from judging the earlier expectation with hindsight.

long_form_passage_analyses.stylistic_notes: Separate channels before synthesis; describe model updates as information-set revisions rather than retroactive proof that the prior estimate was irrational.

long_form_passage_analyses.stylistic_notes: Explain transformations before presenting model results so the reader can see what comparability was created and what heterogeneity remains.

long_form_passage_analyses.location: Model validation and conclusions, Chapters 8–9, printed pp. 26–29

structure: reject one model while retaining another

observations.observation: Model validity is output-specific: a framework can fit distributions adequately while failing for contributions, so one component's failure should not become a global validity label.
Mean-path fit and distribution/quantile calibration answer different validation questions; a single accuracy label can conceal failure on one of them.

long_form_passage_analyses.stylistic_notes: Name the output that validates or fails; preserve mixed evidence rather than averaging it into a single verdict.

long_form_passage_analyses.location: Discussion and limitations, Chapter 10, printed pp. 30–31
long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: Use model failure to identify an omitted temporal structure without overstating the proposed mechanism.

observations.observation: A model's systematic failure can reveal a missing lifecycle feature, such as an early contribution lag, without implying that the underlying cash-flow phenomenon is absent.
A practitioner narrative that could explain an observed lag is a mechanism hypothesis, not an identified causal mechanism; prose should retain that epistemic status.

long_form_passage_analyses.stylistic_notes: Treat explanatory narratives as hypotheses unless separately identified; use model misspecification as information rather than as a reason to erase the observed pattern.

long_form_passage_analyses.stylistic_notes: Attach uncertainty to the stage where it enters the chain and trace its downstream consequence rather than adding a detached generic caveat.

long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: Separate estimated allocation values from observed prices and condition recognition timing on satisfaction/control criteria.

observations.observation: In a staged analytical pipeline, downstream allocation and measurement inherit upstream classification choices; uncertainty or error can propagate rather than reset at each stage.
When stand-alone selling prices are unavailable and must be estimated, summaries should label them as estimated/model-based inputs rather than observed market facts.
Over-time versus point-in-time revenue recognition is conditional on the relevant satisfaction/control criterion; timing should be stated with the criterion that justifies it.

long_form_passage_analyses.stylistic_notes: Keep estimated inputs linguistically distinct from observed prices; make the recognition criterion part of the sentence when it controls timing.

long_form_passage_analyses.location: Robustness of the IFRS 15 framework, Chapter 6.3.4, printed pp. 278–280

observations.observation: A rule, classification, or execution process can change when an outcome is recognized without changing its cumulative total over the full horizon; period timing and cumulative amount are separate analytical claims.

long_form_passage_analyses.stylistic_notes: When timing moves but total-period amount does not, name the timing effect directly instead of describing it as an increase/decrease in the underlying economic total.

long_form_passage_analyses.stylistic_notes: Treat disclosure as evidence about observability and interpretation, not automatically as evidence that the underlying economic state improved.

long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: Decompose downstream effects of interpretation and preserve industry/business-model conditioning.

Industry and business-model conditions belong in the conclusion when they determine which recognition issues are material; a standard-wide observation should not be universalized across firms.

long_form_passage_analyses.stylistic_notes: Separate presentation/timing effects from underlying business change and keep industry/business-model qualifiers attached to the claim.

universal_analytical_candidates.name: Level versus change/intervention
universal_analytical_candidates.learned_pattern: A variable's level and an imposed change in that variable are different evidentiary objects and can support different or opposite outcome relationships.
universal_analytical_candidates.boundary_or_condition: The level and the intervention/change must be separately observed or defined.

universal_analytical_candidates.name: Baseline state versus shock sensitivity
universal_analytical_candidates.learned_pattern: A group can begin from a worse baseline without responding more strongly to a subsequent shock; baseline disparity and shock elasticity are separate claims.
universal_analytical_candidates.boundary_or_condition: Baseline disparity does not identify response elasticity.

universal_analytical_candidates.name: Decision-time information set
universal_analytical_candidates.learned_pattern: Historical evaluation should use information that was actually available at the decision point; ex-post final outcomes can create hindsight relationships that were not actionable ex ante.
universal_analytical_candidates.boundary_or_condition: Use the information set available at the decision/forecast date; later information may justify revision.

universal_analytical_candidates.name: Transition effect versus enduring regime effect
universal_analytical_candidates.learned_pattern: After a regime change, immediate implementation/transition consequences and persistent steady-state consequences are different claims; a short-run effect should not automatically be described as permanent.
universal_analytical_candidates.boundary_or_condition: The transition window and later regime must be distinguished by horizon.

universal_analytical_candidates.name: Balance-sheet stock versus underlying transaction flow
universal_analytical_candidates.learned_pattern: An observed financing stock or structure can be changed by different underlying transactions. Outstanding debt, loan-balance growth, new issuance, refinancing, and drawdown of a pre-existing commitment should not be treated as the same flow.
universal_analytical_candidates.boundary_or_condition: Identify which transaction flow changed the balance-sheet stock before assigning mechanism.

universal_analytical_candidates.name: Two-sided transaction outcome decomposition
universal_analytical_candidates.learned_pattern: A negotiated financing outcome such as quantity, price, maturity, or channel usage can jointly reflect borrower demand/constraints and lender or supplier willingness/capacity. The observed outcome should not be assigned to one side without decomposition.
universal_analytical_candidates.boundary_or_condition: Requires evidence capable of separating borrower and lender/supplier channels for one-sided attribution.

universal_analytical_candidates.name: Upstream commitment or booked state versus downstream realization
universal_analytical_candidates.learned_pattern: An upstream commitment, order, booking, or other expected-output state is not the same as downstream realized output. Conversion depends on intervening execution/fulfillment, so upstream evidence should not automatically acquire realized revenue, cash, or output language.
universal_analytical_candidates.boundary_or_condition: Conversion from commitment/booked state to realization requires intervening execution or fulfillment.

universal_analytical_candidates.name: Current state versus adjustment velocity
universal_analytical_candidates.learned_pattern: A system's current level and the speed/path with which it is changing toward another level are different analytical objects. A snapshot cannot substitute for a measured adjustment process.
universal_analytical_candidates.boundary_or_condition: A snapshot cannot substitute for a measured/estimated path of adjustment.

universal_analytical_candidates.name: Contractual trigger changes control architecture
universal_analytical_candidates.learned_pattern: A contractual or rule-based threshold can change who holds decision or control rights before the underlying system reaches full failure or default; crossing the trigger changes the governance state and therefore the interpretation of subsequent behavior.
universal_analytical_candidates.boundary_or_condition: The trigger's actual contractual rights must be known; threshold crossing is not synonymous with default.

universal_analytical_candidates.name: Recognition or realization timing versus cumulative amount
universal_analytical_candidates.learned_pattern: A rule, classification, or execution process can change when an outcome is recognized or realized without changing its cumulative total over the full horizon. Period timing and cumulative amount are separate analytical claims.
universal_analytical_candidates.boundary_or_condition: A timing shift and a cumulative-amount change must be measured separately over a defined horizon.

finance_conditioned_language_families.name: Internal funding and working-capital capacity
finance_conditioned_language_families.discipline: Distinguish internally generated cash capacity from cash balances, borrowing capacity, and realized investment.

finance_conditioned_language_families.name: Cash buffers and precautionary liquidity
finance_conditioned_language_families.discipline: Treat cash as a stock that can buffer outflows without implying it is costless, permanent, or committed to one use.

finance_conditioned_language_families.name: Debt stock, issuance, refinancing, and drawdown
finance_conditioned_language_families.discipline: Keep balance-sheet stock distinct from the transaction flows that change it.

finance_conditioned_language_families.name: Borrower demand and lender credit-supply capacity
finance_conditioned_language_families.discipline: Treat observed financing outcomes as potentially two-sided unless the design separately identifies borrower and lender channels.

finance_conditioned_language_families.name: Credit price, maturity, rollover, and contractual control
finance_conditioned_language_families.discipline: Separate financing price, quantity, tenor, refinancing risk, and governance triggers.

finance_conditioned_language_families.name: Funding-source substitution
finance_conditioned_language_families.discipline: Describe movement across funding channels without assuming every substitution is involuntary financial constraint.

finance_conditioned_language_families.name: Private-capital commitment and cash-flow lifecycle
finance_conditioned_language_families.discipline: Order the lifecycle from contractual commitment through actual cash movements; commitment is not paid-in capital.

finance_conditioned_language_families.name: Private-capital realized and residual value
finance_conditioned_language_families.discipline: Distinguish realized cash returned from residual/unrealized value and from cumulative net cash position.

finance_conditioned_language_families.name: Contract, backlog, performance obligation, and recognition lifecycle
finance_conditioned_language_families.discipline: Keep booked/upstream commercial states distinct from fulfillment and recognized revenue.

finance_conditioned_language_families.name: Revenue, margin, profit, and cash realization
finance_conditioned_language_families.discipline: Do not equate recognized revenue with margin, recurring economics, or cash collection.

finance_conditioned_language_families.name: Primary and secondary corporate-bond conditions
finance_conditioned_language_families.discipline: Separate issuance-market access from secondary-market pricing/liquidity and broader financial conditions.

finance_conditioned_language_families.name: Current leverage, target leverage, and adjustment speed
finance_conditioned_language_families.discipline: A leverage snapshot and the path/speed of movement toward a target are different claims.

finance_conditioned_language_families.name: Direct liquidity effects and spillovers
finance_conditioned_language_families.discipline: Separate direct treatment/exposure from indirect network or counterparty transmission.

finance_conditioned_language_families.name: Asset allocation and competing uses of funds
finance_conditioned_language_families.discipline: Describe allocation among uses of funds without treating one balance-sheet category as the sole motive or causal mechanism.

evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.name: Meta-analytic pooled evidence
evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.appropriate_expression: Lead with the pooled direction only after separating constructs; retain heterogeneity, publication-bias, and design dependence when material.

evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.name: Quasi-experimental or policy-shock evidence
evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.appropriate_expression: Use causal or effect language only for the identified margin and attach treatment, timing, and population boundaries.

evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.name: Observational balance-sheet relationships
evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.appropriate_expression: Use association/relationship language; do not infer financing mechanism from co-movement alone.

evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.name: Two-sided borrower/lender outcomes
evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.appropriate_expression: Use neutral outcome language until borrower demand and lender supply are separately identified.

evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.name: Accounting recognition and measurement evidence
evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.appropriate_expression: Separate reported recognition/timing/classification effects from underlying business economics; label estimates and judgments.

evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.name: Transition or adoption regime evidence
evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.appropriate_expression: Separate implementation-period effects from persistent regime effects and avoid extrapolating one transition window.

evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.name: Private-fund performance metrics
evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.appropriate_expression: State realized and unrealized components separately; preserve vintage, strategy, lifecycle, and valuation boundaries.

evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.name: Forward commitment, order, and backlog evidence
evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.appropriate_expression: Use upstream-state language and identify the execution/fulfillment conditions required before realization.

evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.name: Primary versus secondary bond-market evidence
evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.appropriate_expression: Keep issuance access/terms separate from secondary spread/liquidity evidence and from aggregate financial conditions.

evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.name: Dynamic adjustment models
evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.appropriate_expression: Report current state, target/reference state, and adjustment speed/path separately; model parameters are not direct transaction observations.

evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.name: Covenant and contractual-trigger evidence
evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.appropriate_expression: Describe threshold crossing as a governance/control-state change; do not equate it automatically with default or total failure.

evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.name: Proxy and disclosure evidence
evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.appropriate_expression: Name what the disclosed/proxy measure actually observes and preserve coverage/visibility limits; more disclosure is not automatically more information.

evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.name: Stochastic/model-based private-capital forecasts
evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.appropriate_expression: Use forecast/model/estimate language, validate outputs separately, and attach sample, calibration, and contract-state assumptions.

evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.name: Qualitative expert and implementation evidence
evidence_conditioned_expression_mappings.appropriate_expression: Use perception/experience/interpretation language for interview evidence; distinguish available discretion or plausible mechanisms from observed use or causal effect.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Level → change/intervention separation
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: State the baseline level; then separately state the change, intervention, or shock; compare their outcome relationships only after the objects are distinct.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Baseline state → shock response
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: Describe pre-shock condition first; then describe response magnitude or elasticity; do not infer one from the other.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Balance-sheet stock → transaction-flow decomposition
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: Name the observed stock; identify issuance, refinancing, repayment, or drawdown flows that can change it; avoid using one flow as a synonym for the stock.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Commitment → call/execution → realization
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: Order the sentence or paragraph from contractual commitment through cash call/execution to realized cash/output; preserve any remaining commitment.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Financing outcome → borrower/lender decomposition
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: State the observed quantity/price/maturity/channel outcome, then distinguish borrower demand/constraint from lender willingness/capacity.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Transition → later regime
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: State the immediate implementation response, then the later recovery or steady-state behavior; label the horizon of each.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Price + quantity + maturity + channel
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: When financing conditions are multidimensional, synthesize the relevant dimensions rather than treating a single spread or quantity as the whole condition.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Realized + residual value decomposition
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: Lead with cash returned when realization is the question; then state residual/unrealized value and total-value metrics without collapsing them.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Current state → target/reference → adjustment velocity
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: Separate the current level from the target/reference and from the estimated speed/path of convergence.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Contractual trigger → control-right change → subsequent behavior
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: Identify the threshold, the governance/control rights it reallocates, and only then the behavior observed after the trigger.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Contract/order → obligation → fulfillment/control → revenue → cash
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: Preserve the commercial realization chain; recognized revenue and cash collection appear only after their own conditions.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Result → mechanism candidate → limitation
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: State the identified result first, introduce mechanism language at the strength supported, and attach the specific limitation to that mechanism claim.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Null/mixed result → bounded conclusion
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: State what was not detected or where signs differ; avoid rewriting lack of evidence as evidence of absence.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Funding-channel substitution
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: Name the constrained or changed channel, the alternative channel used, and the evidence for substitution; preserve voluntary-strategy alternatives when unresolved.

sentence_and_argument_architectures.name: Timing shift → cumulative amount distinction
sentence_and_argument_architectures.pattern: State whether recognition/realization moved across periods; separately state whether the cumulative amount over the full horizon changed.

verb_and_predicate_families.name: Direct observation
verb_and_predicate_families.use: For measured/descriptive evidence; choose association verbs when identification is observational.

verb_and_predicate_families.name: Identified effect
verb_and_predicate_families.use: Reserve for designs that identify the stated causal margin and keep the treatment/population boundary.

verb_and_predicate_families.name: Financing access/capacity
verb_and_predicate_families.use: Tie the verb to the correct borrower/lender or transaction object.

verb_and_predicate_families.name: Commitment and realization
verb_and_predicate_families.use: Use lifecycle-specific verbs so upstream states do not acquire downstream predicates.

verb_and_predicate_families.name: Adjustment
verb_and_predicate_families.use: Use only when a dynamic path is observed/estimated; do not turn a snapshot into a movement verb.

verb_and_predicate_families.name: Control/governance
verb_and_predicate_families.use: Name the contractual threshold and the right/control change separately from default.

verb_and_predicate_families.name: Model/forecast
verb_and_predicate_families.use: Keep model-generated quantities linguistically distinct from observed cash flows or market transactions.

verb_and_predicate_families.name: Evidence limitation
verb_and_predicate_families.use: Use claim-specific limitation language rather than generic hedging.

verb_and_predicate_families.name: Null or mixed evidence
verb_and_predicate_families.use: Preserve the difference between non-detection, absence, and heterogeneity.

finance_domain_language_characteristics: Finance prose is lifecycle-sensitive: commitment, funding, execution, recognition, distribution, residual value, and cash realization are different stages.
Stocks and flows must remain separate: cash and debt balances are not the transactions that change them.
Financing outcomes are often two-sided; borrower demand and lender/supplier capacity can jointly determine quantity, price, maturity, and channel.
Realized and unrealized private-market value require different nouns and predicates.
Credit conditions are multidimensional: access, quantity, spread, maturity, liquidity, covenant state, and refinancing conditions should not be flattened into one 'tight/easy' label.
Current state and adjustment path are separate: leverage, liquidity, and other balance-sheet states can be high/low while adjustment speed differs.
Commercial evidence is staged: contract/order/backlog precedes fulfillment/control, recognized revenue, margin, and cash collection.
Accounting/reporting transitions can move recognition timing or classification without an equivalent change in underlying business economics.
Boundary conditions such as firm size, borrower/lender type, vintage, industry, crisis regime, maturity, and information set frequently belong in the main claim.
Numbers should establish the relationship or decomposition, not organize the prose as a metric recital.

anti_patterns.name: Level/change collapse
anti_patterns.avoid: Using a variable's level and a change/intervention in that variable as grammatical substitutes.

anti_patterns.name: Baseline/shock collapse
anti_patterns.avoid: Inferring stronger shock sensitivity merely because a group starts from a worse baseline.

anti_patterns.name: Debt stock/flow collapse
anti_patterns.avoid: Calling outstanding debt, issuance, refinancing, repayment, and committed-facility drawdown the same financing event.

anti_patterns.name: Commitment/realization collapse
anti_patterns.avoid: Treating capital commitments, booked demand, or backlog as realized cash, output, or revenue.

anti_patterns.name: Revenue/cash collapse
anti_patterns.avoid: Treating recognized revenue as cash collection or as proof of margin/profit realization.

anti_patterns.name: Realized/unrealized value collapse
anti_patterns.avoid: Treating NAV/RVPI as cash returned or treating TVPI as if it were fully realized performance.

anti_patterns.name: Borrower/lender attribution collapse
anti_patterns.avoid: Assigning an observed loan quantity, price, or maturity entirely to borrower demand or lender supply without identification.

anti_patterns.name: Primary/secondary bond collapse
anti_patterns.avoid: Using issuance conditions and secondary-market spreads/liquidity as interchangeable market states.

anti_patterns.name: Maturity/total-debt collapse
anti_patterns.avoid: Inferring rollover risk or tenor from total debt alone.

anti_patterns.name: Current/target/adjustment collapse
anti_patterns.avoid: Treating current leverage, target leverage, and speed of adjustment as one construct.

anti_patterns.name: Trigger/default equivalence
anti_patterns.avoid: Describing a covenant/control threshold crossing as full economic default unless default itself is observed.

anti_patterns.name: Transition/permanent-regime collapse
anti_patterns.avoid: Generalizing an implementation-period effect into a permanent steady-state effect.

anti_patterns.name: Hindsight substitution
anti_patterns.avoid: Evaluating a historical financing decision using outcomes or information unavailable at the decision point.

anti_patterns.name: Proxy reification
anti_patterns.avoid: Treating a disclosure, ratio, or model estimate as the underlying construct without naming the proxy boundary.

anti_patterns.name: Aggregate-to-individual inference
anti_patterns.avoid: Using aggregate credit or fund evidence to assert an unobserved individual borrower, issuer, or company condition.

anti_patterns.name: Association-to-causation inflation
anti_patterns.avoid: Upgrading observational co-movement or time alignment into structural causal language.

anti_patterns.name: Partial-mechanism completion
anti_patterns.avoid: Turning mediation, moderator, or plausible mechanism evidence into proof of a complete causal channel.

anti_patterns.name: Regime/subgroup generalization
anti_patterns.avoid: Dropping horizon, vintage, borrower type, lender type, geography, or regime when it changes the result.

anti_patterns.name: Null-to-absence inversion
anti_patterns.avoid: Rewriting 'no evidence of X' as evidence that X is absent.

anti_patterns.name: Disclosure-volume/informativeness collapse
anti_patterns.avoid: Treating more disclosed material as automatically more decision-useful information.

unresolved_and_contested_patterns.issue: Borrower demand versus lender supply identification
unresolved_and_contested_patterns.note: Many observed financing outcomes remain jointly determined unless the design isolates one side.

unresolved_and_contested_patterns.issue: Bond spread, liquidity, and credit-risk composition
unresolved_and_contested_patterns.note: Observed spreads can combine credit, liquidity, risk appetite, and market-structure components; evidence design determines how far decomposition is justified.
NAV/RVPI remain valuation-based residual states; distributions/DPI are realized cash states.
Conversion depends on fulfillment, cancellation, performance obligations, and recognition rules; no universal conversion rate should be implied.
High cash can reflect precaution, transaction needs, financing constraints, investment timing, or strategic choice.
The consequences of maturity composition vary with refinancing conditions, credit access, and borrower state.
Rights and responses after a trigger vary across contracts and lenders; the trigger itself is not a universal failure state.
Recognition timing/classification can change reported-period outcomes without an equivalent change in underlying commercial economics.
Substitution can reflect constraint, relative price, maturity preference, relationship structure, policy support, or voluntary strategy.

transferable_observations.observation: A system can preserve baseline output while reconfiguring internal parameters: more functional release sites can coexist with lower release probability, changing the response to burst inputs without requiring the same change in steady baseline transmission.
Resource quantity and resource utilization probability are separate state variables; increasing one while decreasing the other can produce a qualitatively different transfer function.
Short-term facilitation and longer-term plasticity can change together but operate on different timescales, so the time horizon is part of the mechanism description.
A measured behavioral improvement can align with several concurrent structural and signaling changes; convergent mechanism evidence should not be compressed into a single uniquely proven pathway.

A useful analogy preserves the features that are genuinely shared and explicitly leaves non-shared features unresolved.

transferable_observations.observation: Acquisition, consolidation, and reconsolidation are distinct process phases; an intervention's meaning depends on when in the process it occurs.
Timing can function as identification evidence: perturbing a mechanism in one phase but not another helps determine which process the mechanism participates in.
Multiple pathways can interact to produce one system-level outcome; a synthesis should preserve parallel and convergent pathways rather than force a single-channel story.
A review is stronger when it prioritizes mechanisms linked to the target system-level outcome rather than treating every adjacent molecular effect as equally explanatory.

transferable_observations.observation: A total resource pool can remain stable while the relationship between local components changes materially; aggregate stability does not imply structural stasis.
Components sharing an upstream connection can still vary independently at the local interface; common origin does not guarantee synchronized local state.
Pre- and post-synaptic structures can adapt differently and on different timelines, illustrating asynchronous adjustment inside one functional unit.
A group average can conceal distinct local structural classes; system interpretation may require unit-level or component-level heterogeneity.

Structural observations can rule in plausible mechanisms and rule out simplistic isolation assumptions while leaving actual dynamic function unresolved.
Distributed elements need not be spatially centralized to behave as a coordinated system if topology provides shared inputs or coupling points.

transferable_observations.observation: A complex causal chain is easier to reason about when each transformation is validated separately: source signal, classifier/controller, physical transmission, intermediate messenger, and final output.
Thresholding converts a continuous input into a discrete control action; analysis should distinguish the input magnitude from the controller's state transition.
Signal encoding and biological output are distinct stages; a successful upstream classification does not by itself establish downstream actuation.
A reversible control architecture should describe activation, persistence, deactivation, and recovery rather than only the ON state.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Coupled state-variable decomposition
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: Aggregate system behavior can be decomposed into multiple state variables or component flows whose interaction, not any one component, determines the observable outcome.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Use as analytical grammar when Finance evidence separately supplies cash, debt, commitments, revenue, spreads, or realized/unrealized value. Do not compress several supplied state variables into a single invented 'financial strength' construct.

canonical_bonus_families.name: State-dependent parameters
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: Rates, sensitivities, probabilities, and effective coefficients can depend on the current state rather than remain fixed.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: When Finance evidence shows condition-dependent sensitivity, phrase the relationship conditionally rather than extrapolating one coefficient across all states.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Multiple time constants and transient versus steady state
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: Different components of one system can respond and recover on different timescales; an initial response and a steady-state response can therefore differ in sign, magnitude, or mechanism.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Reinforces Finance's distinction among immediate funding shock, transition cost, maturity/rollover horizon, and persistent financing condition.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Perturbation rate matters
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: The path and speed of a perturbation can change the system response even when the eventual endpoint is similar.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Use only when Finance evidence includes timing or rate-of-change: an abrupt refinancing or credit change and a gradual one should not be assumed equivalent merely from endpoints.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Thresholds and qualitative state transitions
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: Crossing a threshold can move a system into a qualitatively different response regime; subthreshold and superthreshold behavior are not always linearly scaled versions of each other.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Do not invent financial thresholds. But when supplied evidence establishes a covenant, liquidity, rating, or other threshold, treat crossing it as a state change rather than merely another numeric increment.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Local linearity, global nonlinearity
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: A nonlinear system can behave approximately linearly around a local operating point while requiring nonlinear description farther away.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Reinforces caution against extrapolating relationships measured in ordinary conditions into financial-stress regimes without evidence.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Boundary and control validity
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: A model or measurement is trustworthy only to the extent that the experimental/observational boundary conditions and control assumptions required by it are satisfied.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Strengthens Finance language around proxy construction, data scope, maturity definitions, and the assumptions required to interpret a measured financial state.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Measurement-system interaction and artifact
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: The act or apparatus of measurement can interact with the system and create apparent features that belong to control error rather than to the underlying phenomenon.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Treat model- or data-construction artifacts as a separate possibility when Finance studies explicitly identify them; do not infer artifacts where none are documented.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Feedback and closed-loop architecture
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: Closed-loop systems contain separate action, feedback, command, error, and correction paths; feedback can alter the future state rather than merely report it.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Useful for describing documented reflexive financing processes or policy/credit feedback loops while preserving the direction and evidentiary strength of each path.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Compensation can mask deterioration
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: A compensating component can preserve aggregate function temporarily while another component deteriorates, so stable output need not imply stable internals.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: When Finance evidence shows cash buffers, alternative funding, or lender support offsetting deterioration elsewhere, articulate both the preserved output and the compensating channel.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Heterogeneous response classes and bifurcation
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: A population can split into qualitatively different response classes rather than vary smoothly around one representative average.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Reinforces subgroup, lender/borrower, rating, lifecycle, and leverage-distribution language when Finance evidence reveals distinct response classes.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Static snapshot ambiguity
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: The same static appearance can arise from different trajectories; repeated observations or flow decomposition may be required to know whether a system is growing, shrinking, recovering, or merely stable.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Directly reinforces Finance's stock-versus-flow rule: outstanding debt, cash, NAV, or backlog cannot reveal the underlying transaction path without time/flow evidence.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Phase-specific intervention
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: An intervention can have different meaning depending on whether it acts during formation, consolidation, maintenance, disruption, or recovery.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Useful for maintaining distinctions among contracted demand, current commitment, capital outlay, revenue recognition, cash collection, refinancing, and repayment stages when the Finance evidence supplies them.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Structure supports mechanism hypotheses, not automatic functional proof
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: Anatomical, structural, or topological evidence can make a mechanism plausible without directly demonstrating the system-level function attributed to it.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Reinforces the existing rule that financing structure or network position can support a mechanism interpretation without proving its effectiveness.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Observable state versus latent total state
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: Visible, recorded, or displayed variables may omit latent components that remain economically or functionally active.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Reinforces distinctions such as disclosed versus known information, recognized revenue versus contract state, and reported NAV versus realized cash, without inventing unobserved values.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Common endpoint does not imply common path
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: Different populations or processes can reach a similar endpoint through different trajectories, modes, or intermediate states.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: A similar leverage, liquidity, or funding endpoint can arise through different financing paths; preserve issuance, repayment, refinancing, drawdown, and substitution when the evidence distinguishes them.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Balance variables and asymmetric perturbation
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: Ratios and balances can carry system-level information, but increasing one side and decreasing the other need not produce mirror-image effects.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Supports careful interpretation of coverage ratios, leverage ratios, cash-flow coverage, or borrower/lender balance metrics when directional asymmetry is empirically established.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Model success is not mechanism truth
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: A model can reproduce or predict a wide range of observations while its microscopic or causal interpretation remains tentative.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Reinforces separation of predictive usefulness, descriptive fit, and causal mechanism in Finance models.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Recovery, reversibility, and path dependence
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: A system can recover after perturbation, but recovery may follow different kinetics or a different path from deterioration.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Encourages time-path language for deleveraging, liquidity rebuilding, spread normalization, refinancing recovery, or revenue realization when such evidence is supplied.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Interface transformation chain
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: A signal can pass through multiple interfaces and encodings; each stage can preserve, distort, threshold, delay, or amplify information.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Useful for tracing documented transmission chains such as policy -> lender -> borrower or contract -> accounting recognition -> cash collection, while testing each link separately.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Saturation and information throughput
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: More raw input or activity can push a system into saturation, reducing marginal information transfer or discriminability.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Use only where Finance evidence actually shows saturation or diminishing information/value; do not infer it merely from large levels.

canonical_bonus_families.name: Stochastic threshold and divergent trajectories
canonical_bonus_families.learned_pattern: Random variation can be a plausible source of divergent paths when a system has thresholds or unstable states, but stochastic explanations require evidence rather than rhetorical convenience.
canonical_bonus_families.finance_transfer: Supports calibrated language around probabilistic regime change or default/stress transitions when the Finance source itself supplies stochastic or threshold evidence.
